subject: Benchmark plan & run alignment for Trillio Health onboarding
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Kaplan <ari.kaplan@trilliohealth.com>
Cc: Sarah Ng <sarah.ng@trilliohealth.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmark plan & run alignment for Trillio Health onboarding

Hi Ari / Sarah —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is the initial benchmark plan we discussed (onboard-benchmark-plan.xlsx). Goal here is a short, repeatable pre-prod run that demonstrates we meet your latency and throughput targets before we schedule production canary traffic.

High-level asks from Trillio we captured:
- Target P95 latency: <= 250 ms (text generation, 512-token context)
- Sustained throughput: 120 req/s across the service boundary (client-side concurrency ~8)
- Burst capacity: 250 req/s for 2 minutes

What I'm proposing:
1) Quick sync to confirm traffic shapes and auth hooks (this week).
2) Runbook-driven load test in your pre-prod on Thursday 2026-06-25 (2-hour window).
3) Results and artifacts exchanged; Redwood provides a concise results packet and suggested config adjustments.

Please confirm the targets above and whether the 6/25 window works for you. If we need to move, we can pick the 28th instead.

Attachments: [Attachment: onboard-benchmark-plan.xlsx (15 KB)]

Thanks —
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Benchmark plan & run alignment for Trillio Health onboarding

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the plan and clear summary. Confirming the targets are what we expect from product — P95 <=250ms, sustained ~120 req/s. A couple of clarifications before we lock the window:

- Our pre-prod cluster is behind a staging API gateway that will add ~20ms. Are you comfortable including that in the run profile?
- Auth: we will provide a short-living token; please confirm Redwood will accept bearer tokens for the run.
- We have a downstream service that occasionally back-pressures at high throughput — can Redwood's runbook include a traffic ramp-down step if we see error rates rising?

6/25 works for us (morning Pacific). We prefer a 10:00–12:00 PT window.

Ari Kaplan
Head of Engineering
Trillio Health
ari.kaplan@trilliohealth.com

Ari —

All good notes. Short answers: yes, include the staging gateway in the profile (we'll add a 20ms fixed latency to expected numbers); we support bearer tokens for test traffic; and our runbook includes automated ramp-down on error-rate >2.5% or 5xx spike.

Confirmed: we're booked for Thu 2026-06-25 10:00–12:00 PT. Monica and Ben from our infra team will be on the call to assist with configuration and to run the Redwood-side collector.

Link to the runbook and pre-test checklist: https://redwood-internal/docs/runbooks/trillio-onboard

Quick checklist for Trillio (please confirm):
- Pre-prod endpoint + test bearer token (will expire 2 hours after issue)
- Expected baseline external latency (gateway) if any
- Test dataset or prompts (we'll use the sample prompts in the attached workbook unless you send a replacement)
- Access for our collector to post telemetry to the agreed S3 bucket (we'll provide a presigned URL)

Attachments: [Attachment: onboard-benchmark-plan.xlsx (15 KB)]

Hannah

Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 16:11:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Redwood infra config for Trillio run (prep)

Hannah / Ben —

Preparing infra checklist for 6/25 run (mv to /runbook notes afterwards):
- Model variant pinned to v2.3 (8-bit quantized) to match pre-prod profile
- Batch policy: dynamic batching with max batch size 16, target latency guard 200ms
- KV cache: warm with 50k prefix entries from sample prompts before load window
- Autoscale window: pre-warm 4 GPUs, allow burst to 8 GPUs for 3 minutes
- Telemetry: high-res p99 sampling enabled; we will stream latencies and token counts to S3

I'll attach the runbook notes pdf after finalizing. Ben, please validate the presigned S3 path when Hannah sends it.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ari Kaplan <ari.kaplan@trilliohealth.com>, Sarah Ng <sarah.ng@trilliohealth.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Post-run: Trillio load test results (pre-prod 2026-06-25)

Team —

We ran the scheduled window on 2026-06-25 (10:00–11:40 PT). Quick summary and attached artifacts (load-test-results-20260629.csv, runbook-notes.pdf).

Summary metrics (generation, 512-token context):
- Sustained throughput target: 120 req/s — achieved 125 req/s over 40 minutes (steady state), CPU/GPU utilization within expected range.
- Burst: reached 255 req/s for 90s during the scheduled burst stage, no significant error spike.
- Latency (observed): P50 = 82 ms, P95 = 238 ms, P99 = 412 ms (the latter during an upstream cache miss event).
- Error rates: averaged 0.4% 5xx across the run; two brief spikes when a downstream service returned 503s — runbook ramp-down triggered and mitigated quickly.

Notes & recommended configuration tweaks:
1) Increase KV cache pre-warm to 100k prefixes for production canary to reduce P99 noise around cold-key misses.
2) Maintain dynamic batching, but cap max batch size to 12 for regions with tighter SLOs.
3) Schedule production canary at 50% traffic for 6 hours with telemetry retention for 30 days; Redwood can orchestrate rollback at the 10-min or 3-sig threshold.

Next steps for signoff:
- Trillio: confirm you accept these results as expected evidence for onboarding acceptance.
- Redwood: we'll prepare the final acceptance packet (artifact + annotated results) and propose canary dates once you confirm.

Attachments: [Attachment: load-test-results-20260629.csv (1.2 MB)], [Attachment: runbook-notes.pdf (45 KB)]

Thanks everyone — great collaboration.

Ben Carter
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
